extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing affidavits of resignation (exclusion on consent), alleged practitioner misconduct, publication of discipline, and reinstatement under USPTO rules (37 C.F.R. and relevant statutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) and set forth that: consent is freely and voluntarily rendered; the respondent is aware a disciplinary complaint is pending and of its allegations; the respondent understands the OED Director's opinion regarding alleged violations; the respondent understands the consequences of requesting and consenting to exclusion; and the respondent consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document lists specific acknowledgments the affidavit included: (1) consent freely and voluntarily rendered, not coerced; (2) awareness of a disciplinary complaint pending and that it alleges misconduct in representation of clients before the USPTO; (3) awareness that OED Director believes specific violations of Disciplinary Rules occurred (the order enumerates those violations); (4) acknowledgement that for reinstatement proceedings the OED Director will presumptively treat the pending allegations as true and that respondent could not have successfully defended; (5) affirmation of having read and understood 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60; and (6) consent to exclusion. Approval of the affidavit results in exclusion on consent effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to keep clients reasonably informed / 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not allow a client's patent application to become abandoned without the client's knowledge or consent and must keep the client reasonably informed as to the status of the application and inform the client of critical Office correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order details alleged failures: (i) allowing an individual client's application to become abandoned by failing to inform/respond and not keeping the client reasonably informed or informing her of critical Office correspondence; (ii) allowing a corporate client's patent applications to become abandoned similarly through lack of communication and failure to respond to attempts to communicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify client of significant Office correspondence / 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must notify a client or former client of correspondence received from the Office that could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, or timely notify the Office of inability to notify the client when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule applies when: (i) the correspondence could have a significant effect on a pending matter, (ii) was received by the practitioner on behalf of the client, and (iii) a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances that the client should be notified. The order alleges failure to inform client/former client or timely notify the Office of inability to notify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to refund unearned fees / 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) via § 10.23(c)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must refund fees when appropriate; failing to refund fees owed to a client or former client violates the disciplinary rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order alleges respondent did not refund fees to Hypersolar, Inc. in connection with applications he was hired to prepare and file on its behalf. The citation links general fee-refund duties to the misconduct alleged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Notices, payments, and revival obligations / 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must respond appropriately to Notices of Missing Parts, Notices of Abandonment, Notifications Concerning Payment of Prescribed Fees, Invitations to Pay Prescribed Fees (with late payment), and Notifications that an international application is considered withdrawn; must pay required filing fees; and must seek to revive applications when appropriate to avoid abandonment or withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order lists specific alleged failures: (i) failing to respond to a Notice of Missing Parts, Notice of Abandonment, and failing to seek revival for an individual's application; (ii) not paying the $110 statutory basic filing fee for a corporate client's application, causing abandonment; (iii) not paying $4,467 in prescribed filing fees for a patent application resulting in withdrawal, including failure to respond to successive fee-payment notices and notifications that an international application was considered withdrawn. These acts are treated as violations of § 10.84(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment/Desertion of clients / 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not abandon a client; abandoning a client may be evidenced by omissions and acts that cause the client's applications to become and remain abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order alleges abandonment of both an individual and a corporate client as shown by omissions that caused their applications to become and remain abandoned. This conduct is cited as violating § 10.84(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern of intentional/habitual violations / 37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentional and habitual violations of Disciplinary Rules constitute separate grounds for discipline under the disciplinary regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director was of the opinion that the respondent 'intentionally and habitually' violated Disciplinary Rules, and § 10.89(c)(6) is cited in support of disciplinary action. The order treats such a pattern as an aggravating factor supporting exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption for reinstatement proceedings (37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner who submitted an affidavit of resignation applies for reinstatement, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining reinstatement, that the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged this presumption in his affidavit; the order reiterates that this presumption will apply when deciding any reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60. This affects the standard and evidence required for seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations following exclusion (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27(b), 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following approval of an affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent, the OED Director must publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish notice in the Official Gazette; the OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where practitioner is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order orders publication in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette and instructs the OED Director to notify disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State of admission, courts where admitted, and the public, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59. The order includes an explicit 'Notice of Exclusion on Consent' text to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties upon exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner excluded from practice before the USPTO must comply fully with the obligations set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties/obligations following disbarment/exclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically orders the respondent to 'comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' While the order does not restate § 11.58's text, it imposes the obligations of that regulation as continued requirements (e.g., addressing client files, notice obligations, and other duties prescribed by § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedural obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO must comply fully with the reinstatement requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs respondent to 'comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.' Although not detailed in the Order, § 11.60 governs the procedure and substantive showing required for reinstatement, including fitness to resume practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authority to approve exclusions (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has statutory and regulatory authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and order exclusion on consent from practice before the Office under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these statutes and regulations as the legal basis for approving the Affidavit of Resignation and ordering exclusion on consent. The authority governs the Office's power to discipline, exclude, and publish disciplinary actions concerning registered patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative handling of pending complaints after exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon approval of an affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent, the OED Director shall move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen days of the Final Order's date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly commands the OED Director to move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen days, and states that the OED Director and respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
